candidates.title: Remove inactive sections from a video

demandEvidence.chore: Remove still or inactive sections from a video.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Show HN: demotime: a web app for removing still/inactive sections out of a video

ease.reason: A mock can mark quiet spans in a sample clip, but the post gives no editing method or implementation reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: video editors might pay to reduce manual trimming; this launch post establishes no buyer or willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype could flag candidate spans in sample clips; reliable detection and editing remain unproved.

autonomy.reason: Detection could be repeated on supplied clips, but a person must review cuts and export the result.

evidence.reason: The launch title names inactive-section removal, but gives no task frequency, constraints, or demonstrated workflow.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: concrete proposed clip-trimming task, but no supplied implementation evidence and limited demand detail.

candidates.title: Summarize weekly AI agent runs

demandEvidence.chore: Summarize runs per agent for a team lead on a weekly schedule.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Schedule Trigger (weekly): summarize runs per agent for the team lead.

ease.reason: A sample run log and weekly summary are a bounded mock, but no source documents the data path or implementation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams operating several agents might pay for run summaries; the request establishes no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can summarize operator-provided fictional run records; real agent logs and formats are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: A weekly summary can be generated from supplied records, while a lead must check accuracy and investigate issues.

evidence.reason: The request specifies weekly per-agent run summaries, but not recurrence evidence, input fields, or implementation support.

candidates.reason: Below threshold and duplicate: the proposed buyer group, teams operating AI agents, overlaps the recent agent-operations post 0d455200b5ff2b5b39d4eac6.

candidates.title: Export AI chats to common files

demandEvidence.chore: Export multiple AI chat conversations to Notion, Markdown, or PDF.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Show HN: AIExportHub – bulk export AI chats to Notion, Markdown, and PDF

ease.reason: A manual sample export can test one destination, but no supplied source documents export mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: consultants handling many AI chats might pay for portable archives; the post establishes no paid demand.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can transform a small supplied transcript set; destination APIs and format edge cases remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable conversion could prepare files, while a person checks omissions and authorizes destination access.

evidence.reason: The launch title names bulk export and three destinations, but provides no task frequency or working evidence here.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: specific export idea, but no implementation reference and no evidence of an unmet or recurring service need.

candidates.title: Send an email after an app trigger

demandEvidence.chore: Send an email through an SMTP service when another app trigger occurs.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want a Make scenario to send an email through DigitalAka when a trigger occurs in another app.

ease.reason: A test trigger and operator-controlled inbox define a small experiment, though integration steps are unsupported.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small business needing triggered notifications might pay for setup; the request proves neither a buyer nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can use synthetic events and a test inbox; authentication and provider compatibility remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: A trigger can prepare a test message, but a person must verify recipient, content, permissions, and delivery.

evidence.reason: The request names the trigger-to-email task and provider, but offers no successful run or repeated-use evidence.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: concrete task, but no supplied implementation reference supports the SMTP integration.

rejected.reason: The excerpt says only that the author is working on adding AI agents to Jira-like workflows; it does not state a concrete notification chore. No assigned implementation reference is available. A notification task would be invented.

rejected.title: Get guidance using Make automations
rejected.reason: The exact excerpt says only “I’m new to Make.com and looking for guidance.” It names no concrete chore or requested service, so a specific experiment and demandEvidence task cannot be supported.

rejected.title: Evaluate an existing document-based assistant
rejected.reason: The excerpt asks for firsthand experiences from people who hired an evaluator; it does not identify an evaluation task or method. A scored prototype would invent the requested work.

rejected.title: Find the supported Cloudflare R2 signer setup
rejected.reason: The excerpt asks a one-off technical configuration question. It does not support a recurring service workflow or a bounded repeatable business experiment.

rejected.title: Create a multi-axis political spectrum mapper
rejected.reason: The launch title describes a product, not a concrete chore or request for service. The excerpt supplies no task evidence from which to scope a demand-backed experiment.

steps.message: Assessed all nine assigned discussion identities. Five concrete tasks received provisional five-criterion scores; each is below the 6.0 threshold, and the agent workflow also overlaps recent post 0d455200b5ff2b5b39d4eac6. Four vague or one-off items were excluded with their literal evidence limits. No implementation references were supplied; no post is proposed.
